summary: Heeraman Tiwari is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the universities of Lucknow, Delhi, and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal and Richard Gombrich. He held positions at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~2000), Heidelberg University (2011–2012), and the Israel Institute for Advanced Studies (2014–2015).
Hege Myrlund Larsen is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She earned her PhD at the University of Bergen (attested 2009) under the supervision of Bruce Kapferer.
Hegoda Khemananda is a Buddhist studies scholar. In 1993, he is attested as Vice Principal at Vidyodaya Pirivena and Director at Dharma Paryeshanalaya.

Heidi Fjeld works in Tibetology and other fields. She studied at the University of Oxford and the University of Oslo under Signe Howell (~2001–2006), later serving as a postdoctoral fellow at Oslo (~2006–2010).

Heidi I. Koppl is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her MA at the University of Copenhagen under Christian K. Wedemeyer and also studied under the traditional teacher Sherab Zangpo.

Heidi Rika Maria Pauwels works in Indology and religious studies. She studied at KU Leuven, Vrindaban Research Institute, University of Cologne, and University of Washington under Alan Entwistle. She taught at SOAS (1994–1996) before becoming Professor at the University of Washington (1996, 2002).

Heike Oberlin is an Indologist who studied at Kerala Kalamandalam and the universities of Tübingen and Würzburg. She held positions at Tübingen (2005–2008), Kerala Kalamandalam (2018), and Sapienza University of Rome (2025).
Heiner Eichner was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg under Karl Hoffmann (~1964–1974) and held a post at the University of Vienna (~1989–2010).
Heinrich August Jäschke was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He served as co-director at Moravian Schools Niesky (1847) and as a missionary for the Moravian Church (1857–1868).

Heinrich Blochmann was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies and history. He studied at Leipzig under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer, Paris under Karl Benedikt Hase, and Calcutta. His career included posts at Fort William College, Doveton College, and Aliah University.
Heinrich Brunn was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at the University of Bonn (~1839–1843). He held an academic post at the University of Munich (~1865–1894).

Heinrich Ewald worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Eichhorn, Tychsen, and the Plancks. He held posts at Große Schule (1822–1824), Göttingen (1824–1837, 1848–1867), and the University of Tübingen (1838–1848).
Heinrich Gustav Hotho worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1822–1826) and later held a post there (~1829–1873).

Heinrich Hettrich was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Saarland, Giessen, and Munich, and held posts at Saarland, Munich, Salzburg, Zurich, Marburg, and Würzburg, where he was Chair of Comparative Linguistics from 1989.

Heinrich Hübschmann worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Jena under August Schleicher, Tübingen, Leipzig, and Munich under Martin Haug. He held posts at the University of Leipzig (1876) and the University of Strasbourg (1877).

Heinrich Kiepert was a historian, archaeologist, and geographer. He studied at Frederick William University and the University of Jena under August Boeckh and Julius Heinrich Petermann. He held positions at Landes-Industrie-Comptoir (1845–1852) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1854, 1874).

Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann and in Paris under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Antoine-Léonard Chézy, later holding a chair at Leipzig from 1836.

Heinrich Lüders was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist. He studied at Munich and Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn. He held posts at Oxford, Göttingen, Rostock, Kiel, and Humboldt University of Berlin (1909–1935), also serving as secretary of the Prussian Academy of Sciences.

Heinrich R. Zimmer was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Wilhelm Schulze (~1909–1913) and held posts at the University of Greifswald (~1920–1924) and Heidelberg University (~1924–1938).

Heinrich Rickert was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1884–1885) and the University of Strasbourg (~1885–1888). He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (~1891–1916) and Heidelberg University (~1916–1932).
